items.title: 61428_Red Callender oral history interview
items.q: we worked together... I worked with a lot of piano players who I loved dearly, but the two that I seemed to get along with best would be Gerry Wiggins

ctx.x: Oh, probably a couple of years off and on, we worked together. And I have to say that the two joys of my life would Tatum and Gerry Wilson...I mean, Gerry Wiggins. You know, I worked with a lot of piano players who I loved dearly, but the two that I seemed to get along with best would be Gerry Wiggins, number one, because I'm freer with him... With Tatum, it wasn't a case of being free, it was a case of being a good accompanist for whatever he did. Does that make sense?
Of course. It was really enjoyable seeing you at your concert in March '82 here, and it was a grand reunion. There was Gerry Wiggins, there was Bill Douglass...
